History:
• Main complaint: Profuse watery diarrhoea for 3 days, occurring approximately hourly when awake.  
• Onset/Duration: Began Monday/Tuesday (≈3 days ago); ongoing.  
• Character/Progression: Watery, no blood; associated with intermittent mid-lower abdominal cramp preceding each episode (≈6/10 pain, comes and goes).  
• Associated symptoms: Nausea; occasional vomiting (noted once after milk). Feels febrile/“burning up” (no documented measurement). Passing urine less frequently. No reported throat swelling or other systemic symptoms.  
• Exposures: Brother experiencing similar illness for 5 days; no known food triggers or recent travel.  
• Diet/Intake: Able to ingest fluids; feels they “go straight through.” Last solid food at lunch today—passed loosely.  
• Previous episodes: None reported.

Past Medical History:
• Chronic illnesses: None reported.  
• Surgical/Hospitalisations: Not mentioned.  
• Medications: Paracetamol as needed (dose/route/frequency not documented). No regular medications.  
• Allergies: No known drug allergies.  
• Family history: Father with stage III colon cancer.  
• Social history: Lives with mother and sister. Office job (government) in Central London. Social smoker (occasional cigarettes, mostly Fridays). Alcohol: 1 beer on weekdays; heavier intake 1–2 ×/month (binge).  

Physical Examination:
• Teleconsultation—limited exam.  
   – General: Alert, conversant on video. Able to sit comfortably; no distress reported.  
   – Abdomen: Reports intermittent mid-lower cramping; location midline; no focal lateralisation.  
   – No visible blood in stool by history.  
   – Reports subjective fever; vitals not measured.  
   – Hydration: Reports high diarrhoeal losses; urine output decreased but present.  

Impression:
Acute infectious gastroenteritis with risk of dehydration.

Management Plan:
• Oral rehydration therapy: Recommended over-the-counter Dioralyte; encourage clear fluids.  
• Diet: Start with clear fluids, progress to soft diet (soup, mashed foods) as tolerated.  
• Symptom control: Paracetamol for fever/abdominal discomfort.  
• Lifestyle: Avoid alcohol until recovered; continue to rest from work as needed.  
• Safety-net: If symptoms worsen or fail to improve within 48 hours (ongoing high stool frequency, persistent vomiting, inability to keep fluids, signs of dehydration), patient to call back or seek urgent care for further evaluation (possible labs, IV fluids, stool studies).  
• Follow-up: Telephone review if not improving in 1–2 days.

Patient Summary:
27-year-old man with 3-day history of hourly watery diarrhoea, abdominal cramps, mild nausea/vomiting, and subjective fever—likely acute gastroenteritis, possibly shared household contact. Advised oral rehydration, soft diet, symptomatic relief, and to recontact if no improvement or deterioration.

Key Takeaways:
1. Start Dioralyte and maintain high fluid intake to prevent dehydration.  
2. Use paracetamol for fever or pain; avoid alcohol.  
3. Seek medical review if diarrhoea persists beyond 48 hours, vomiting increases, or signs of dehydration develop.

Next Steps:
• Monitor symptoms and hydration status over next 48 hours.  
• Re-consult GP if no improvement; may require in-person assessment, vitals, bloodwork, or stool culture.  
• Consider stool sample and further GI evaluation if persistent or if red-flag features (blood, severe pain, weight loss) arise.

Quality checks (document_quality):
• Missing expected elements: No vitals (BP, HR, temperature), no objective abdominal exam findings, no medication reconciliation beyond paracetamol.  
• Internal conflicts: None noted.  
• Transcript quality: Generally clear audio; minor interruptions but clinically adequate information obtained.
